Plan: Fix TypeScript errors in permissions.ts

**Root Cause:**
The `getCurrentUser` function has overloaded signatures for `QueryCtx` and `ActionCtx`, but when called with a union type `CtxForAuth = ActionCtx | QueryCtx`, TypeScript cannot match the overload.

**Solution:**
1. Remove the overloaded signatures (lines 89-90)
2. Keep only the single implementation signature that accepts `QueryCtx | ActionCtx`
3. The implementation already correctly handles both types

**Why this works:**
- The overload resolution fails with union types
- The implementation signature already properly accepts `QueryCtx | ActionCtx`
- This is a common pattern in TypeScript - use union types directly instead of overloads when the caller might have a union type

```typescript
// Returns all students in game with submission status

  userId: id,
  name: string,
  email: string,
  companyId: id,

}
```

- Join with companies for company names

- Aggregate presence data from @convex-dev/presence

```typescript
// Students who haven't submitted in X days
{
  userId: id,
  name: string,
  companyId: id,
  companyName: string,
  daysSinceLastActivity: number,
  lastActivityType: "hiring" | "leadership" | "never",
}
```

# Context: Why This Bead Exists

**Current State:**
- Auth is completely broken: `convex/auth/config.ts` has `providers: []`
- This causes blank /login page and blocks all E2E tests
- User has Mailgun account and prefers it over Resend (pricing model concerns)
- Previous magic link setup used Resend but was disabled

**Decision:**
After reviewing [Convex Auth docs](https://labs.convex.dev/auth/config), magic link is:
- ✅ Simplest implementation of all methods (per docs)
- ✅ Passwordless (no password hashing, reset flows)
- ✅ Good UX - users click email link to sign in

**Research Findings:**
- Convex Auth built on [Auth.js](https://authjs.dev) (formerly NextAuth.js)
- Mailgun supported via [`Email()`](https://labs.convex.dev/auth/api_reference/providers/Email) provider
- Custom email provider via `sendVerificationRequest` function
- Can use Nodemailer or Mailgun API directly

# Implementation Tasks

## 1. Create Mailgun Email Provider
File: `convex/auth/MailgunOTP.ts` (new)
- Use \`@convex-dev/auth/providers/Email\` 
- Implement \`sendVerificationRequest\` using Mailgun API
- Generate 6-digit OTP code (use \`@oslojs/crypto\` or \`crypto.getRandomValues\`)
- Send email from configured domain

Required env vars:
- \`AUTH_MAILGUN_API_KEY\` - Mailgun private API key
- \`AUTH_MAILGUN_DOMAIN\` - Verified Mailgun domain
- \`AUTH_MAILGUN_FROM\` - From address (e.g., "My App <noreply@myapp.com>")

## 2. Enable Provider in Auth Config
File: \`convex/auth/config.ts\`
- Import MailgunOTP provider
- Add to \`providers\` array in \`convexAuth()\`
- Keep existing callbacks intact

## 3. Update Login Form
File: \`src/routes/login.tsx\`
- Change provider from \`"resend"\` to \`"email"\` (or custom provider ID)
- Ensure form sends \`email\` and \`redirectUrl\` params
- Handle sign-in flow correctly

## 4. Set Environment Variables
- Add Mailgun credentials to Convex dashboard (Settings → Environment Variables)
- Or use \`npx convex env set AUTH_MAILGUN_* <value>\`

## 5. Deploy & Test
- \`npx convex deploy\`
- Test magic link flow end-to-end
- Run E2E test: \`npm run test:e2e tests/e2e/e2e-01-browser.test.tsx\`

# Reference Implementation Pattern

See [Password reset with Resend](https://labs.convex.dev/auth/config/passwords) for similar pattern - replace Resend SDK with Mailgun SDK or \`fetch\` calls to \`https://api.mailgun.net/v3/{domain}/messages\`.

# Success Criteria
- ✅ User can enter email on /login
- ✅ Magic link/OTP sent via Mailgun
- ✅ User clicks link/enters code and is authenticated
- ✅ E2E-01 test passes (browser mode)
- ✅ No Resend dependency remaining

# Dependencies
- \`npm install @oslojs/crypto\` (for secure token generation) - optional
- Or use native \`crypto.getRandomValues()\`
- Mailgun account with verified domain

# Notes
- Integration tests already passing (7/7) - they use \`convex-test\` in-memory
